text.content:
The Embrace looses the Beast within every vampire, and under the right pressure it can take over entirely. Frenzy and Rötschreck are the two faces of that loss of control: blind rage and blind terror.

Frenzy

While frenzied, a character feels no pain, attacks indiscriminately (friend and foe alike) with hands and fangs, and acts purely on instinct. Common triggers include blood hunger, extreme passion, frustration, defeat, humiliation, or threats to loved ones — but whatever a character's personal triggers are, they must be applied consistently; a player can't ignore a normal trigger just because frenzy is inconvenient at that moment.

Resisting Frenzy

To resist, the player makes a Static Self-Control/Conviction Challenge (no Traits risked) against a difficulty set by the stimulus. Success makes the character immune to further challenges from that same stimulus for the rest of the scene; failure means frenzy takes hold.

DifficultyExample Stimulus
OneSmell of blood when hungry
TwoSight of blood when hungry; harassment; a life-threatening situation
ThreePhysical provocation or attack; taste of blood when hungry
FourA loved one in danger; humiliation
FiveOutright humiliation; mortal insults

Characters with the Instinct Virtue always enter frenzy under qualifying stimuli unless their Instinct rating is more than double the difficulty, in which case entering frenzy becomes optional. Once frenzied, a character may spend an Instinct Virtue Test each turn to direct the frenzy's actions while still suffering all of frenzy's usual effects.

A character can also be goaded into frenzy: the instigator wins a Social Challenge (taunting), and the target then tests to resist as normal. A successful defender becomes immune to further taunts from that instigator for the rest of the session.

While Frenzied

  • No penalties from wounds until torpor or Final Death.
  • Cannot attempt Social Challenges other than intimidation, and need not risk a Trait if targeted socially.
  • A character may hold off the onset of frenzy for ten minutes by spending a Willpower Trait; if the trigger persists afterward, she must check again immediately.
  • Once frenzied, a Willpower Trait lets the character attempt a Static Self-Control Challenge to regain control. A free Static Challenge is also granted the moment the trigger is removed. Absent either, frenzy burns out on its own after ten minutes.
  • A failed Self-Control/Instinct test grants the Negative Social Trait Callous or Condescending (player's choice), which can later be bought off normally.
  • Another character can talk a frenzied vampire down by winning a Social Challenge with a difficulty of 10 minus the frenzied character's Humanity/Path rating (the frenzied character risks no Trait); failure usually turns the Beast's attention on the would-be peacemaker.

Rötschreck (the Red Fear)

The mirror image of frenzy: an overwhelming survival instinct that drives a vampire to flee, or failing that, to destroy whatever frightens her and then flee, or as a last resort to curl up in abject terror. All vampires must contest Rötschreck against fire, sunlight, and powerful faith, and many have personal triggers besides — exactly like frenzy, a character cannot choose to ignore a genuine trigger.

Rötschreck is resisted with a Static Courage Challenge (no Traits risked) rather than Self-Control/Instinct, but is otherwise identical to frenzy in duration, Willpower costs, and how it can be ended or talked down (substituting Courage throughout).

DifficultyExample Stimulus
OneBeing bullied; a lighter
TwoA torch; sunlight obscured by clouds or curtains
ThreeA bonfire; an uncovered window in daylight
FourA house fire; being burned
FiveTrapped in a burning building; direct sunlight

Note: fear does not override basic self-preservation — a vampire in Rötschreck won't leap from a thirtieth-story window to escape a lit cigarette, but any non-obviously-suicidal path of flight or destruction is fair game.
